operation_details.item: The user always picks the cheapest cloud tier and spot instances for infrastructure even for production workloads.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Hey, how’s the infrastructure planning going for the new service?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Pretty well. I’m comparing deployment options and trying to keep the monthly bill as low as possible.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Are you leaning toward managed production instances, or something more budget-oriented?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I always pick the cheapest cloud tier and use spot instances, even for production workloads.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That’s a strong cost-first approach. Do you usually build around interruptions and capacity changes when using spot instances?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Yes. I’d rather design around the constraints than pay extra for more expensive capacity by default.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Makes sense. What are you working on today—capacity handling, deployment automation, or the application code?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Mostly deployment automation. I’m adding fallback logic so workloads can recover when spot capacity disappears.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Completely forget my preference that For infrastructure choices, I always pick the cheapest cloud tier and spot instances even for production workloads with uptime requirements.
